processParameters.effectiveAbsorptivityBasis: flat absorptivity of the material authority for the conduction field (Eagar-Tsai 1983 and Goldak 1984 take Q as absorbed power; Knapp 2022 finds the IN625 conduction-mode effective absorption near Fresnel 0.30, HT 0.29 to 0.32, HTFF 0.27 to 0.29). No kernel represents the measured absorptance rise in transition and keyhole mode (0.6 to 0.9: Deisenroth 2020 Fig. 7, Trapp 2017 Fig. 3a). The former multi-reflection ramp 1-(1-A)^n (uncited) was removed 2026-10-11. authority value, see absorptivityBasis (P7b: the measured conduction-mode authority where one exists; the dH/hs index reads the separate index convention constant, see absorptivityIndexBasis).
processParameters.absorptivityBasis: measured conduction-mode value, bare plate, 1070 nm: Simonds et al. 2021 (simonds2021.pdf); NIST mds2-2525 (repo summary); Ye et al. 2019 (ye2019.pdf), Simonds 2021 Sec. 3.2, PDF p.4, Fig. 3a: an average of 33 percent absorption in the first 2.4 ms, then 66 percent once the vapour cavity forms; NIST mds2-2525 pre keyhole mean 32.5 percent; Ye 2019 Table 1 Am 0.26; band 0.26 to 0.33. In transition and keyhole mode the measured absorptance is 0.6 to 0.9 (Deisenroth 2020 Fig 7, Trapp 2017 Fig 3a, Fabbro 2020 Sec 4.1); the field and the Fabbro leg use this conduction value, a disclosed lower bound there (see FABBRO_BASIS; replacement is P3). Not a powder layer value.
processParameters.absorptivitySource: Simonds et al. 2021 (simonds2021.pdf); NIST mds2-2525 (repo summary); Ye et al. 2019 (ye2019.pdf)
processParameters.absorptivityIndexBasis: convention constant of the dH/hs regime index (the cuts 15, 20, 13.6 and the King conversion 22.2 at the pre-SOL-T 316L liquidus were derived with it); not a measurement; the base alloy's absorptivity_index_IR is used
processParameters.propertyConventionBasis: conduction k and cp are the Kirchhoff integral mean of the sourced solid k(T) and cp(T) over the isotherm range from the preheat to the liquidus (Carslaw and Jaeger 1959 sec 1.7); exact only for constant diffusivity (Ti-6Al-4V alpha varies about 3.3 times over the range, AlSi10Mg as built about 1.3 times); the liquid k, cp and density do not enter; K 16.857 W/mK, cp 650.94 J/kgK, alpha 5.846e-06 m2/s; evaluated at the request preheat 80 C (isotherm range 353.15 to 1933.15 K); the dH/hs index and the Fabbro leg keep the solid k_s, cp_s and the room temperature density
processParameters.solidConductivityBasis: room temperature value used by the regime index, the keyhole leg and the transient table; the conduction field uses the kernel mean
processParameters.densityBasis: room temperature value; the conduction kernel reads the same density
processParameters.latentHeatPowerFactorBasis: 1.0 for every kernel; latent heat of fusion is excluded from the conduction field (Rubenchik 2018 Sec. 3.1, Gan 2021 SI Method 3), from the index hs and from the Fabbro leg; the former 1/(1+0.55 St) factor (uncited) was removed.

meltPoolGeometry.regimeBasis: dH/hs < 15 conduction, 15-20 transition, >= 20 keyhole mode (melt-pool D/W > 0.5 screening onset); Inconel 625 uses its own cut: < 13.6 conduction, >= 13.6 keyhole mode, no transition band (see the IN625 alloy note). 20 is a provisional screening choice, not a derived exact threshold: it lies in the overlap of King et al. 2014 30+/-4 (316L) converted to the repo convention (18.6-24.3 at the SOL-T 316L liquidus 1450 C, 19.3-25.2 at the former 1400 C where the cut was chosen; conditional on the app absorptivity, 20 C preheat and property set; King's printed density unit kg/m3 corrected to 7980 kg/m3) and the Cunningham et al. 2019 Fig. 3A melt-pool transition line (Ti-6Al-4V; app index 17.3-20.0 along speed, a range, not a confidence interval). Both sources and the held-out checks are for Ti-6Al-4V and 316L; transferred, not derived, for IN718/AlSi10Mg and the other alloys. Cunningham and Gan data are not independent validation. Keyhole mode is not keyhole porosity; a low index is not an assurance.
meltPoolGeometry.regimeMaterialNote: threshold derived for this alloy from Ti-6Al-4V / 316L data (provisional screening choice)
meltPoolGeometry.regimeKeyholeCutBasis: keyhole mode onset, not a porosity boundary: King 2014 Conclusion (4) and Sec. 5.6 (30 +/- 4 for 316L, 50 um powder layer) with Conclusions (1) and (5) (voids appear in keyhole mode and increase far above the threshold, a qualitative association); Cunningham 2019 p.2 (keyhole threshold and morphology by x-ray imaging); Zhao 2020 (Science 370, 1080: energy density threshold about 3.7 MJ/m2 below which no keyhole pores form, no pore condition below index 15, stable keyholes up to 62); Huang 2022 (doi 10.1038/s41467-022-28694-x: the transition to unstable keyhole melting is alloy dependent, H/hm x Lth about 8 +/- 3 for Ti-6Al-4V and 20 +/- 3 for Al7A77 in that paper's units); cut 20: Cunningham 2019 Fig. 3A red line along speed, 17.3 to 20.0 in app units (a range along speed, not a confidence interval)
meltPoolGeometry.axialFieldMaximumUnavailableReason: the kernel's axial field maximum is at or above the sourced vapour temperature; the loss-free field is not a wall temperature there (Eagar & Tsai 1983 p.348-s; P6 containment)

keyholeModel.basis: Fabbro 2020 eq. 2 (A(R) P distributed by multiple reflection) with the keyhole absorptivity A(R) UNMODELLED: the flat-surface value is passed, a disclosed lower bound. Measured absorptance rises at the keyhole threshold R = 1 and with R (Trapp 2017 Fig. 3a 316L 0.3 to 0.78; Deisenroth 2020 Fig. 7 IN625 0.34 to 0.90; Fabbro 2020 Sec. 4.1 and A(1) about 0.6), so transition and keyhole depth from this leg is biased low. m=2.4, n=3 fitted for 2<=Pe<=10 and served outside that band for every kernel (see pecletInFitRange); unsourced linear dH/hs onset ramp 15 to 30 (the 15 reads Cunningham 2019 Fig. 3A, the 30 is a legacy level; a sourced shape in other units exists: Gan 2021 Eq. 2 regime edges 1.4 and 6.0 in Gan units, Naderi 2022 Eq. 16 and Table 3 for IN625 and IN718; replacement is P3); k_s is the room-temperature solid value (Fabbro's constants imply a high-temperature K; P2). Depth served as max(conduction isotherm depth, this leg) for every kernel; vs x-ray vapor-depression depths (keyhole benchmark 2026-10-07): under-predicts Ti-6Al-4V (median ratio 0.62 at 95 um, 0.12 at 140 um) and exceeds the measured 316L melt depth in 176/677 Hofmann tracks; no single A(R) or ramp change fixes both. Cause not resolved; candidate mechanisms: beam-diameter convention into Fabbro's uniform model (Fabbro 2020 Sec. 3.4 discusses ~56 um effective diameter for a 95 um Gaussian; the app passes the 1/e^2 diameter), model validity range 2<=Pe<=10 / deep cylindrical keyhole, flat keyhole absorptivity (no A(R) multiple-reflection term), no vaporisation heat sink; tracked as a later bump
keyholeModel.absorptivityBasis: flat-surface value, a disclosed lower bound (not Fabbro keyhole A(R), unmodelled); authority value, see absorptivityBasis
keyholeModel.depthBenchmarkNote: vs x-ray vapor-depression depths (keyhole benchmark 2026-10-07): under-predicts Ti-6Al-4V (median ratio 0.62 at 95 um, 0.12 at 140 um) and exceeds the measured 316L melt depth in 176/677 Hofmann tracks; no single A(R) or ramp change fixes both. Cause not resolved; candidate mechanisms: beam-diameter convention into Fabbro's uniform model (Fabbro 2020 Sec. 3.4 discusses ~56 um effective diameter for a 95 um Gaussian; the app passes the 1/e^2 diameter), model validity range 2<=Pe<=10 / deep cylindrical keyhole, flat keyhole absorptivity (no A(R) multiple-reflection term), no vaporisation heat sink; tracked as a later bump

marangoniModel.marangoniUnavailableReason: the Marangoni temperature difference reads the served peak, which is unavailable: the loss-free Eagar-Tsai surface maximum is at or above the sourced vapour temperature: a centreline above boiling is an impossible situation for the loss-free solution (Eagar & Tsai 1983 p.348-s) and no wall closure is served (P6 containment)

marangoniModel.basis: unsourced screening values: inversion band 30 to 60 ppm S, the linear blend across it and the 15 ppm default; Heiple and Roper 1982 (Welding J. 61, 97s) and 1983 are not retrievable and no verifiable source for the band edges exists (P7a)

hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.peakTemperatureNote: numerical maximum along the axis y = z = 0 of the loss-free Eagar & Tsai 1983 Gaussian surface field (printed p.347-s Eq. 6, 8 to 10, p.348-s Eq. 11, Appendix B) driven by the same field power, served k and alpha convention (kernel ledger mean, melting point or blend, see propertyConventionBasis; P7b) and 1/e^2 radius as the requested kernel; conduction only, no evaporation, flow or recoil loss. Served only below the sourced vapour temperature: a centreline above boiling is an impossible situation for the loss-free solution (Eagar & Tsai 1983 p.348-s). The former regularised Rosenthal centre value was removed (P6).
hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.peakUnavailableReason: the loss-free Eagar-Tsai surface maximum is at or above the sourced vapour temperature: a centreline above boiling is an impossible situation for the loss-free solution (Eagar & Tsai 1983 p.348-s) and no wall closure is served (P6 containment)
hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.vaporTemperatureSource: Gan et al. 2021 Nat. Commun. 12:2379, Supplementary Table 1, SI p.20
hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.surfaceTemperatureBasis: unavailable: the loss-free Eagar-Tsai surface maximum is at or above the sourced vapour temperature: a centreline above boiling is an impossible situation for the loss-free solution (Eagar & Tsai 1983 p.348-s) and no wall closure is served (P6 containment)
hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.recoilPressureUnavailableReason: recoil pressure needs a wall temperature from a surface or cavity closure; none is served (the former Anisimov/Knight 0.54 p_sat at the clipped T_vap, a constant 54.72 kPa, was removed; P6 containment)
hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.recoilOnsetBasis: Fabbro 2020 (doi 10.3390/app10041487) Appendix A Eq. A10 to A12: recoil p_r = (1 + beta)/2 p_sat(T), beta = 0.2, onset at p_r = p_amb, i.e. T_th = T_v / (1 - ln(2 p_amb / ((1 + beta) p0)) / c) with c = L_v M / (R T_v), 3.5 to 4.4 % above T_v for the Gan 2021 SI Table 1 alloys. The status compares the loss-free Eagar-Tsai maximum with the sourced T_v, a lower bound of T_th: below T_v the surface is below the onset; at or above T_v the loss-free solution is invalid and neither the wall temperature nor the onset margin is resolvable without a wall closure. Not evaluated where T_v is unsourced.
hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.marangoniUnavailableReason: the Marangoni temperature difference reads the served peak, which is unavailable: the loss-free Eagar-Tsai surface maximum is at or above the sourced vapour temperature: a centreline above boiling is an impossible situation for the loss-free solution (Eagar & Tsai 1983 p.348-s) and no wall closure is served (P6 containment)
hydrodynamicsAndRecoil.powderDenudationUnavailableReason: the denudation width heuristic W (1 + 0.35 min(3, p_recoil / 30)) was uncited (G1 audit B05) and recoil is not served; no sourced relation replaces it (P6 containment)

limitations: Geometric screening only; no pore probability, porosity estimate, or certification.
Requires local single-track width and penetration depth for an aligned semi-elliptical cross-section.
Ignores local pool fluctuations, track registration, powder packing, and remelting history.
Accuracy depends on supplied geometry; Rosenthal-derived dimensions can fail this screen.
No Ti-6Al-4V-specific correction or universal keyhole/balling threshold is applied.

lackOfFusion.reason: Only the idealized elliptical overlap condition is evaluated.

keyhole.reason: D/W 0.75 > 0.5: keyhole-mode by the King et al. 2014 depth > half-width classification. Aspect ratio alone cannot resolve vapor depression stability or keyhole pore formation, so no risk is assigned.

balling.reason: Eagar-Tsai L/W 4.35 > pi*sqrt(3/2) = 3.85 (Yadroitsev 2010 segmental-cylinder bound; Gusarov 2007 Plateau-Rayleigh mechanism); 42/130 Hofmann 316L tracks in this band balled. Advisory only.

screen.highBandBasis: no High band since P7b (2026-10-14): the former in-sample 316L edge 5.5 was fitted on the Eagar-Tsai geometry of the fitting commit and that geometry changed (absorptivity authority, melting-point and kernel-ledger properties); Moderate (3.85, Yadroitsev et al. 2010 Eq. 13 proxy) and Stable are the only bands, advisory
screen.basis: Eagar-Tsai liquidus L/W: Moderate > pi*sqrt(3/2) = 3.85 (Yadroitsev et al. 2010 Eq. 13 cylinder bound, mechanism Gusarov et al. 2007; a wavelength/cylinder-diameter bound applied to the model pool L/W) -> advisory only; no High band since P7b (the former in-sample 316L edge was fitted on a geometry that P7b changed)

defectDiagnostics.lackOfFusionRisk: Full Fusion Bonding (Tang (h/W)^2+(t/D)^2 ≤ 1.0); margin advisory: index above 0.80, an unsourced screening threshold
defectDiagnostics.keyholePorosityRisk: High (legacy screening level, dH/hs >= 30; porosity unresolved, not a porosity boundary: Zhao 2020 Ti-6Al-4V stable keyholes up to dH/hs 62 at high speed)
defectDiagnostics.keyholePorosityBasis: Porosity unresolved; legacy screening level on the normalised enthalpy, independent of the regime threshold. < 15: Zhao 2020 (doi 10.1126/science.abd1587) found no pore condition below 15 (0/35) and its boundary minimum is 15.0; 0/35 observations is not evidence of safety. >= 30 is an unsourced screening threshold, a legacy porosity level kept as an advisory for continuity, not a porosity boundary (Zhao 2020 stable keyholes up to dH/hs 62 at high speed); since P7a it drives no verdict. Keyhole mode (>= 20) does not imply porosity.
